title: Introduce credential-attendant and compact iterable shim for Py/TS/Go SDK ergonomics
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: multiple customers hit fragmented ergonomics around token lifecycle and streaming iterators when migrating long-lived streams (chat/llm) between SDKs. This PR introduces a lightweight, in-process "credential-attendant" abstraction and a small compact-iterable shim to harmonize streaming ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goals: (1) provide a single, well-documented credential lifecycle primitive that supports proactive refresh, lease handoff, and fallthrough chain; (2) surface a compact async/pull iterable that reduces ceremony for callers using streaming responses and makes parity easier across languages; (3) ship non-breaking, opt-in defaults and bump SDK versions to include adapters. Summary of changes (high-level): - Add credential-attendant primitive to each SDK with a shared design doc and test vectors. The attendant exposes: acquire(), renew(), release(), and an events callback for lease/expiry windows. Implementations include an in-memory local attendant plus a pluggable adapter for host-managed delegates. - Introduce compact-iterable shim: an ergonomic wrapper around existing streaming client code that yields typed chunks, handles transient auth errors by coordinating with the attendant, and exposes a single `resume()` hook for consumers to request continuation or full restart. - Add a set of retry presets tuned for streaming: SHORT_STREAM, BALANCED_STREAM, and SLOW_STREAM; these wire into the attendant's renew flow so renewals back off gracefully under load. - Update SDK package manifests and changelogs: Python -> 2.7.0, TypeScript -> 1.9.0, Go -> 1.6.0. - Tests: unit + integration harness that replays token expiry scenarios and simulated network flakiness across all three SDKs. - Docs: add usage examples and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (link: https://linear.app/rw/issue/ENG-4271/credential-attendant-design) - [x] End-to-end test harness for token expiry - [x] Compat shims added, opt-in via client config flag - [x] SDK version bumps and changelog entries - [x] QA smoke on staging (streams + long chat sessions) Notes on compatibility and rollout: this is opt-in by default; existing clients are unaffected unless they enable `credential_attendant: true` in their client config. The attendant intentionally keeps a small public surface to avoid coupling. Related: this PR complements prior cross-SDK session work but focuses on minimizing friction for streaming consumers.
